title: Cut generated commit subjects at a word boundary
summary: Replace the three bare `.chars().take(72)` cuts of generated subjects/titles (manage.rs, reading.rs, store.rs) with one shared word-boundary truncation helper, with tests and a CHANGELOG note. Audience: Athena maintainers reading git log.

defaults_applied.how: Helper unit tests plus site-level tests; clippy and fmt clean.
One shared helper replaces all three duplicated truncations.
Tests check cut results, not just that the helper exists.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Goal: generated commit subjects/titles stop ending mid-word; audience is Athena maintainers reading git log.
Helper placed in crates/athena-core/src/commits.rs (existing module, already public), reused by the three sites.
Limit stays 72 chars; trailing whitespace/punctuation trimmed after cut; no ellipsis added.
Other take(N) uses (jev.rs, audience.rs, gate commit ids) are not subjects and stay.

acceptance_criteria.text: Unit tests for the new helper pass under `cargo test`: over-limit text is cut at the last whitespace within 72 chars so no word is split; text at or under the limit is unchanged; a single over-long word is hard-cut at 72 chars; multibyte text does not panic.
A `cargo test` test builds a long intervention subject (manage.rs) and a long reading title (reading.rs) and shows neither ends mid-word and both are at most 72 chars.
The three `.chars().take(72)` sites (manage.rs subject, reading.rs title, store.rs title fallback) call the shared helper instead.
`cargo clippy` is clean, `cargo fmt --check` passes, and the full `cargo test` passes.
CHANGELOG.md notes that generated commit subjects and titles are cut at word boundaries.

out_of_scope: Truncations that are not commit subjects or titles (jev.rs, audience.rs, gate commit ids)
